legal.headline: Shocking: Bombay High Court on not booking MP Parth Pawar in Mundhwa Land Scam despite 99% stake
legal.hook: Shocking: Bombay High Court on not booking MP Parth Pawar in Mundhwa Land Scam despite 99% stake
legal.summary: The Bombay High Court has passed an order declining to initiate criminal proceedings against Parth Pawar, Member of Parliament, in connection with the Mundhwa land scam despite evidence showing he held a 99% stake in the entity involved. The judgment addresses the threshold question of whether sufficient prima facie case exists to book Pawar under criminal statutes. The court's reasoning—apparently accepting arguments that shareholding alone does not establish criminal culpability without direct involvement in the fraudulent transaction—has drawn criticism for what observers characterize as a protection of a high-profile political figure. The order reflects a divergence between civil/corporate liability (where majority ownership typically triggers responsibility) and the criminal threshold courts are applying in property fraud cases involving politicians. No timeline has been reported for any appeal or further investigation.
legal.contextNote: This invokes Section 420 IPC (cheating) and likely Sections 406–409 (criminal breach of trust/dishonesty), where mens rea and direct participation remain essential elements even where shareholding is decisive in civil law. The court has implicitly rejected a *res ipsa loquitur* approach to criminal liability based on control—distinguishing *Ericsson Telecom* (2013, corporate entity liable for acts of directors) by requiring personal knowledge or active direction. For in-house counsel advising on land transactions or fund movements through special purpose vehicles: (1) Ensure decision-making and payment authorization trails are documented separately from shareholding; a 99% owner may escape criminal liability if the transaction was executed by others without their written instruction. (2) Do not rely on corporate structuring alone to shield UBOs in fraud cases—courts now read 'involvement' narrowly, so clean audit trails and independent board minutes become critical. (3) Watch for inconsistency: civil recovery (CIRP, insolvency) may succeed where criminal prosecution fails, so parallel remedies may be necessary.

tech.headline: Fed's Lisa Cook sees AI inflationary push as a top 2027 risk

world.headline: Israel's prime minister says a pilot tried to crash a plane traveling to Tel Aviv
world.hook: One pilot stabbed another pilot on a FlyDubai flight headed to Tel Aviv on Wednesday and may have tried to crash the plane before passengers and crew members subdued him, Israel's prime minister says.
world.summary: On Wednesday, a FlyDubai flight traveling to Tel Aviv experienced a serious incident when one pilot stabbed another pilot, allegedly attempting to crash the aircraft. The incident occurred mid-flight, prompting passengers and crew members to intervene and subdue the assailant. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the event, highlighting the severity of the situation. The flight was diverted safely, and no injuries to passengers were reported. The assailant's motives remain unclear, and investigations are underway. This incident raises significant concerns about airline security and the mental health of flight crew members.

world.headline: Picanha, prices and politics: What Brazil's favorite steak says about the election
world.hook: President Lula promised Brazilians four years ago they'd be able to afford picanha again.
world.summary: Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, seeking re-election, faces criticism over rising picanha prices, a popular beef cut. In 2019, picanha prices were around 40 reais per kilogram; they have since soared to approximately 70 reais. Lula had promised to make picanha affordable again, but the current prices reflect broader economic challenges, including inflation and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. The situation has drawn ire from voters, especially as Lula's government has struggled to stabilize the economy. The price of picanha has become a symbol of the economic discontent among Brazilians, with some voters expressing their frustration through social media. Lula's opponents are leveraging this discontent as a campaign issue, questioning his ability to fulfill his promises. The upcoming elections in October 2024 will serve as a critical test for Lula's administration amidst these economic pressures.
